question_text: State the location and function of the different types of meristems.

page_header: Histology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants · 4 marks

steps.label: Apical meristem
steps.margin_note: Three types, three short blocks. Position first, then the job it does.
lines: Meristems are groups of cells that keep
dividing. On the basis of their position they
are of three types.
Location: at the tip of the root and at the
tip of the shoot.
Function: it adds new cells at the tip, so the
root and the shoot grow in length. This is
primary growth.
Example: root apical meristem, shoot apical
meristem.
steps.why: Naming a meristem is naming its position, so both halves of the answer follow from where the dividing cells sit. Cells at a tip can only add cells ahead of themselves, which is growth in length.
common_mistakes: Giving the location and leaving out the function. The question asks for both.
Saying the apical meristem increases thickness. A tip adds length.
steps.memory_tip: Apex means tip, and tip growth means growth in length.

steps.label: Intercalary meristem
steps.margin_note: Two lines for the position, two for the function, one for the example.
lines: Location: between two permanent tissues,
usually at the base of the internode or at the
leaf base.
Function: it adds length even after the tip
has been removed, so the parts eaten by
grazing animals or cut off grow back.
Example: grasses.
steps.why: Intercalary means placed in between. Because these dividing cells lie behind the tip, the shoot can still add length when the tip itself is gone.
common_mistakes: Placing this meristem at the tip. It lies between permanent tissues, behind the tip.
Leaving out the grass example, which is the one the book gives.
steps.memory_tip: Inter means between. Cut grass grows back because its meristem is not at the tip.

steps.label: Lateral meristem
steps.margin_note: Say secondary growth in words. That is the phrase the examiner looks for.
lines: Location: along the sides of the stem and the
root, lying as a cylinder inside the organ.
Function: it adds cells towards the outside
and towards the inside, so the stem and the
root grow in thickness. This is secondary
growth.
Example: vascular cambium, cork cambium.
steps.why: Lateral means at the side. A cylinder of dividing cells along the flank can only add cells outward and inward, so what it increases is girth, not length.
common_mistakes: Writing that the lateral meristem increases length. Sideways division gives thickness.
Leaving out the two examples. Vascular cambium and cork cambium are the marked ones.
steps.memory_tip: Lateral means side, and side growth means girth. Both cambiums are lateral.

steps.label: Diagram of the three meristems
steps.margin_note: A quick outline with the three labels earns this mark. Two minutes is enough.
steps.why: One shoot outline holds all three positions at once, so the examiner can see that you know where each meristem sits without reading the words again.
common_mistakes: Drawing the lateral meristem as a band across the stem. It runs along the sides.
Leaving the three labels off the sketch.
steps.memory_tip: Draw one shoot: the tip, then a band lower down, then two strips along the flanks.

insider_note: Most students write the three names and stop. The location and the function are separate marks, so give both for each type.
